children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex. Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care - meaning you live with him and/or pay for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I take care of all his needs - his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that, to be honest. I don't know if anyone else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask another question to help clarify the situation:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he also live with anyone else (such as another parent or relative) for part of the time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just one final question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This won't affect whether you can *claim* Child Benefit, but it may affect whether there's a tax charge to pay.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into my income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to understand if I'm eligible to claim in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I have enough information to assess your eligibility for claiming Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me, let me provide my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You're responsible for Alex and he lives with you full-time
- You provide for all his needs
- He's not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation

**One important point to note:** Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. Since Alex lives with you full-time, it's unlikely someone else is claiming, but when you apply, HMRC will check this. If someone else is already claiming for Alex, you'd need to sort that out with them first.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Is there anything else you'd like to know about the process?
